## Sample-level Quality-Control

```{r sample_level}
#| echo: false

raw_metrics <- read_csv(file = csv_metrics, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Normalise a metric value to numeric: drop thousands separators, percent
# signs, and cellranger's "---" placeholder for unavailable values.
clean_numeric <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub(',', '', x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- sub('%', '', x)
  x[x %in% c('---', '', 'NA')] <- NA
  as.numeric(x)
}

if (all(c("Metric Name", "Metric Value") %in% colnames(raw_metrics))) {

  # cellranger multi: long/tidy metrics_summary.csv. Per-sample cell metrics
  # live under Category == "Cells"; metrics not reported per demultiplexed
  # sample (mean reads per cell, sequencing saturation are pool-level and
  # shared across samples) are taken from Category == "Library".
  gex <- raw_metrics %>% dplyr::filter(`Library Type` == "Gene Expression")

  pick <- function(category, metric) {
    v <- gex %>%
      dplyr::filter(Category == category, `Metric Name` == metric) %>%
      dplyr::pull(`Metric Value`)
    if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else clean_numeric(v[[1]])
  }

  sample_metrics <- tibble::tibble(
    `Estimated Number of Cells`  = pick("Cells",   "Cells"),
    `Mean Reads per Cell`        = pick("Library", "Mean reads per cell"),
    `Median Genes per Cell`      = pick("Cells",   "Median genes per cell"),
    `Median UMI Counts per Cell` = pick("Cells",   "Median UMI counts per cell"),
    `Sequencing Saturation`      = pick("Library", "Sequencing saturation")
  )

} else {

  # cellranger count: wide, single-row metrics_summary.csv. Coerce the
  # character measure columns (percentages, comma-grouped counts) to numeric.
  sample_metrics <- raw_metrics %>%
    mutate_if(is.character, clean_numeric)

}

#

check_list <- c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)

#

if(isTRUE(sample_metrics$`Estimated Number of Cells` >= thr_estimate_n_cells)) {
  check_list[1] <- TRUE #300

}

if(isTRUE(sample_metrics$`Mean Reads per Cell` >= thr_mean_reads_per_cells)) {
  check_list[2] <- TRUE #25000

}

if(isTRUE(sample_metrics$`Median Genes per Cell` >= thr_median_genes_per_cell)) {
  check_list[3] <- TRUE #900

}

if(isTRUE(sample_metrics$`Median UMI Counts per Cell` >= thr_median_umi_per_cell)) {
  check_list[4] <- TRUE #1000

}

#

status_flag <- NA

#

if(all(check_list)) {

  status_flag <- "SAMPLE:SUCCESS"

} else {

  if(isTRUE(sample_metrics$`Sequencing Saturation` <= 70)) {

    status_flag <- "SAMPLE:FIXABLE"

  } else {

    status_flag <- "SAMPLE:FAILURE"

  }

}

```

:::{.callout-important}
This sample has been flag as <strong>`r status_flag`</strong>
:::

## Cell-level Quality-Control

```{r seurat_object}

expression_matrix <- Read10X_h5(filename = input_gex_matrices)
seurat_object = CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = expression_matrix,
  project = sample_name
)

# Calculating mitochondrial content

seurat_object[["percent_mito"]] <-
  PercentageFeatureSet(seurat_object, pattern = "^MT-")

gpdat <- tidyr::gather(
  data.frame(
      rname = rownames(seurat_object@meta.data),
      seurat_object@meta.data
    ),
  key = type,
  value = value,
  -rname,
  -orig.ident
  )

ggplot(data = gpdat, aes(x = orig.ident, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = '#f8766d', outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ type, scales = 'free') +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = 'log10') +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.9),
    legend.position = 'none'
  )


```

```{r cell_filtering}

# The subset() calls below overwrite seurat_object, so the pre-filter metadata
# has to be kept now or the QC diagnostics have nothing to plot: every figure
# in this notebook would otherwise describe only the cells that survived, which
# is precisely the population that cannot tell you whether the cut was right.
# sc-best-practices uses "percent counts in the top 20 genes" as a third MAD
# filtering axis alongside counts and genes. A library where a handful of genes
# (MALAT1, mitochondrial, ribosomal) dominate is low-complexity even when its
# total count looks healthy, and neither nCount nor nFeature catches that.
.topn <- 20L
qc_pre <- seurat_object@meta.data
.pct_top <- tryCatch({
  .m <- SeuratObject::LayerData(seurat_object, layer = "counts")
  .tot <- Matrix::colSums(.m)
  # Walk the sparse column pointers directly rather than apply() over columns:
  # a dense per-cell sort would materialise a 30k x 18k matrix.
  .pp <- .m@p; .xx <- .m@x
  .ts <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(.m)), function(j) {
    if (.pp[j + 1] <= .pp[j]) return(0)
    v <- .xx[(.pp[j] + 1):.pp[j + 1]]
    sum(sort(v, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(.topn, length(v)))])
  }, numeric(1))
  100 * .ts / pmax(1, .tot)
}, error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(.pct_top) && length(.pct_top) == nrow(qc_pre)) {
  qc_pre[[paste0("pct_counts_top", .topn)]] <- .pct_top
}

# Which genes dominate the library overall (scater's "top expressed features").
.top_genes <- tryCatch({
  .m <- SeuratObject::LayerData(seurat_object, layer = "counts")
  .gs <- Matrix::rowSums(.m); .gt <- sum(.gs)
  .o <- head(order(.gs, decreasing = TRUE), 20)
  data.frame(gene = rownames(.m)[.o], pct = 100 * .gs[.o] / max(1, .gt))
}, error = function(e) NULL)

n_total_cells <- dim(seurat_object)[2]

seurat_object <- subset(
  x = seurat_object,
  subset = (nFeature_RNA >= thr_n_feature_rna_min & nFeature_RNA < thr_n_feature_rna_max)
  )

#

n_thr_features_cells <- dim(seurat_object)[2]

#

seurat_object <- subset(
  x = seurat_object,
  subset = percent_mito < thr_percent_mito
  )

#

n_observed_cells <- dim(seurat_object)[2]
# Inline `r n_observed_cells` printed as "1.0365^{4}" -- knitr renders a
# scientific-notation number as LaTeX. Format it once, here.
n_observed_fmt <- format(n_observed_cells, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

#

if(status_flag == 'SAMPLE:SUCCESS') {

  if(n_observed_cells >= thr_n_observed_cells) {

    status_flag <- "CELL:SUCCESS"

  } else {

    status_flag <- "CELL:FAILURE"

  }

}

write_lines(status_flag, file = paste0('log/', sub('\\w+:', '', status_flag), '.txt'))

```

## QC diagnostics {#qc-diagnostics}

```{r qc-thresholds, include = FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(ggplot2); library(data.table)})
qcd <- as.data.table(qc_pre)
setnames(qcd, old = intersect(c("percent.mt","percent.mito"), names(qcd)),
              new = rep("percent_mito", length(intersect(c("percent.mt","percent.mito"), names(qcd)))),
         skip_absent = TRUE)

# --- MAD-based thresholds, computed for COMPARISON only ---------------------
# sc-best-practices recommends 5 MADs on log1p(counts) and log1p(genes) and
# 3 MADs on mitochondrial percent, on the grounds that a fixed cutoff applied
# to every sample biases against samples with genuinely smaller cells. This
# notebook does NOT act on them -- changing what gets filtered would silently
# move every downstream result. It reports what MADs would have chosen so the
# decision can be made on evidence rather than on a default.
mad_bounds <- function(x, n_mad = 5, log = TRUE) {
  v <- if (log) log1p(x) else x
  m <- median(v, na.rm = TRUE); d <- mad(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  b <- c(m - n_mad * d, m + n_mad * d)
  if (log) expm1(b) else b
}
# geom_hex() silently requires the `hexbin` package, which is NOT a ggplot2
# dependency; if it is missing the chunk aborts and takes the whole render with
# it. geom_bin2d() is core ggplot2 and needs nothing extra, so fall back to it.
.binlayer <- function(bins = 95) {
  if (requireNamespace("hexbin", quietly = TRUE)) ggplot2::geom_hex(bins = bins)
  else ggplot2::geom_bin2d(bins = bins)
}

mad_feat <- mad_bounds(qcd$nFeature_RNA, 5, TRUE)
# A 5-MAD bound in log space is deliberately lenient and its UPPER end routinely
# lands past the number of genes that exist (the first real run reported
# "9-186452 genes"). Cap it at the transcriptome and record whether either end
# actually binds, so the advisory does not quote an impossible number.
n_genes_total <- nrow(seurat_object)
mad_feat[2] <- min(mad_feat[2], n_genes_total)
mad_feat[1] <- max(mad_feat[1], 0)
mad_hi_binds <- mad_feat[2] < n_genes_total
mad_lo_binds <- mad_feat[1] > min(qcd$nFeature_RNA, na.rm = TRUE)
mad_mito <- mad_bounds(qcd$percent_mito, 3, FALSE)[2]
# Third MAD axis recommended by sc-best-practices: percent counts in top N.
.topn_report <- if (exists('.topn')) .topn else 20L
.topcol <- grep("^pct_counts_top", names(qcd), value = TRUE)[1]
mad_top <- if (!is.na(.topcol)) mad_bounds(qcd[[.topcol]], 5, FALSE)[2] else NA_real_

keep_fixed <- qcd$nFeature_RNA >= thr_n_feature_rna_min &
              qcd$nFeature_RNA <  thr_n_feature_rna_max &
              qcd$percent_mito <  thr_percent_mito
keep_mad   <- qcd$nFeature_RNA >= mad_feat[1] & qcd$nFeature_RNA < mad_feat[2] &
              qcd$percent_mito < mad_mito
n_disagree <- sum(keep_fixed != keep_mad, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r qc-finding, results = 'asis'}
pct_kept <- 100 * sum(keep_fixed, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(qcd)
msg <- sprintf(paste("Of **%s barcodes**, **%s (%.1f%%)** pass the fixed thresholds",
                     "(genes %s-%s, mitochondrial <%s%%). Median depth is **%s UMIs**",
                     "and **%s genes** per cell."),
               format(nrow(qcd), big.mark = ","),
               format(sum(keep_fixed, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ","), pct_kept,
               format(thr_n_feature_rna_min, big.mark = ","),
               format(thr_n_feature_rna_max, big.mark = ","), thr_percent_mito,
               format(round(median(qcd$nCount_RNA, na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ","),
               format(round(median(qcd$nFeature_RNA, na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ","))
if (pct_kept < 50) msg <- paste(msg,
  "**Fewer than half the barcodes survive QC**, which usually means the thresholds",
  "are too aggressive for this sample rather than that the sample is bad.")
scratch_finding(msg, type = if (pct_kept < 50) "caution" else "note",
                title = "Filtering outcome")

pct_dis <- 100 * n_disagree / nrow(qcd)
# Braces are load-bearing: at top level R closes `if (cond) expr` at the
# newline and then fails on a bare `else`.
gene_txt <- {
  if (!mad_hi_binds && !mad_lo_binds) {
    sprintf("**no effective gene limit** (the 5-MAD range spans the whole observed range, %d-%d)",
            round(mad_feat[1]), round(mad_feat[2]))
  } else {
    sprintf("**%s-%s genes**", format(round(mad_feat[1]), big.mark = ","),
            format(round(mad_feat[2]), big.mark = ","))
  }
}
m2 <- sprintf(paste("Adaptive (MAD) thresholds derived from this sample would be",
                    "%s and **mitochondrial <%.1f%%**, versus the fixed",
                    "**%s-%s** and **<%s%%** actually applied. The two rules disagree on",
                    "**%s cells (%.1f%%)**."),
              gene_txt, mad_mito,
              format(thr_n_feature_rna_min, big.mark = ","),
              format(thr_n_feature_rna_max, big.mark = ","), thr_percent_mito,
              format(n_disagree, big.mark = ","), pct_dis)
if (!is.na(mad_top)) m2 <- paste(m2, sprintf(
  paste("A third axis best practice recommends -- percent of counts in the top %d genes --",
        "has a 5-MAD upper bound of **%.1f%%** here (median **%.1f%%**); **%s cells** exceed it.",
        "This is not filtered on at all at present."),
  .topn_report, mad_top, median(qcd[[.topcol]], na.rm = TRUE),
  format(sum(qcd[[.topcol]] > mad_top, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")))
m2 <- paste(m2, "_Advisory only -- filtering used the fixed thresholds._")
if (pct_dis > 10) m2 <- paste(m2,
  "**A disagreement above 10% means the threshold choice is materially shaping this",
  "dataset**, not just trimming its edges. Worth deciding deliberately.")
scratch_finding(m2, type = if (pct_dis > 10) "caution" else "note",
                title = "Fixed vs adaptive thresholds")
```

```{r qc-joint, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# The chapter is explicit that QC metrics must be read JOINTLY: a low-count cell
# with low mitochondrial content is a small cell, while the same count with high
# mitochondrial content is a dying one, and no single-metric histogram separates
# them. Hexbin rather than points because 10k+ overplotted dots hide the density
# that matters -- and it also keeps the figure under the interactive-widget
# size guard, so it stays hoverable.
# Colour each bin by MEAN mitochondrial content rather than by cell count.
# Density alone cannot separate small cells from dying ones; this recovers the
# mito dimension that a coloured scatter would show, without the overplotting
# that makes a scatter unreadable at this cell count.
.summlayer <- function(bins = 95) {
  if (requireNamespace("hexbin", quietly = TRUE))
    ggplot2::stat_summary_hex(ggplot2::aes(z = percent_mito), fun = mean, bins = bins)
  else
    ggplot2::stat_summary_2d(ggplot2::aes(z = percent_mito), fun = mean, bins = bins)
}
ggplot(qcd, aes(nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA)) +
  .summlayer() +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#dbe8fa", high = "#8c1d18",
                      name = "mean\nmito %") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(thr_n_feature_rna_min, thr_n_feature_rna_max),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#8a5a00") +
  labs(title = "Library size vs genes detected",
       subtitle = "dashed = applied gene thresholds; log-log; colour = mean mitochondrial % per bin",
       x = "UMIs per cell", y = "genes per cell") +
  theme_scratch()
```

```{r qc-mito-vs-depth, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
.mito_top <- max(as.numeric(thr_percent_mito) * 1.2,
                 quantile(qcd$percent_mito, 0.995, na.rm = TRUE))
.mito_hidden <- sum(qcd$percent_mito > .mito_top, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(qcd, aes(nCount_RNA, percent_mito)) +
  .binlayer() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7e2d8", high = "#8c1d18", trans = "log10", name = "cells") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = thr_percent_mito, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#8a5a00") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mad_mito, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#0d366b") +
  # Most cells sit below ~20% while a handful of dying cells reach 70%, so a
  # linear axis spends half the panel on near-empty space. Clip the view to the
  # 99.5th percentile (or just above the applied cutoff, whichever is higher)
  # and say how many points that hides -- clipping silently would misrepresent
  # the tail that the cutoff exists to remove.
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, .mito_top)) +
  labs(title = "Mitochondrial content vs library size",
       subtitle = sprintf("dashed = applied cutoff (%s%%); dotted = 3-MAD adaptive cutoff (%.1f%%)%s",
                          thr_percent_mito, mad_mito,
                          if (.mito_hidden > 0)
                            sprintf("; %s cells above %.0f%% not shown",
                                    format(.mito_hidden, big.mark = ","), .mito_top) else ""),
       x = "UMIs per cell", y = "mitochondrial reads (%)") +
  theme_scratch()
```

```{r qc-top-genes, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
# scater's "top expressed features": if a handful of genes hold a large share of
# every library, the dataset carries less biological signal than its cell count
# suggests. MALAT1 and MT- genes at the top of this list are the usual sign.
if (exists(".top_genes") && !is.null(.top_genes) && nrow(.top_genes)) {
  .tg <- .top_genes
  .tg$tip <- sprintf("%s\n%.2f%% of all counts", .tg$gene, .tg$pct)
  # A logical fill renders its legend as FALSE/TRUE; `labels=` on the scale is
  # dropped by ggplotly. Map to a factor with the wanted levels up front so the
  # legend text survives the conversion to a widget.
  .tg$origin <- factor(ifelse(grepl("^MT-", .tg$gene), "mitochondrial", "nuclear"),
                       levels = c("nuclear", "mitochondrial"))
  ggplot(.tg, aes(reorder(gene, pct), pct, fill = origin, text = tip)) +
    geom_col(width = .7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(nuclear = "#3f6fa8", mitochondrial = "#8c1d18"),
                      name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .12))) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Genes taking the largest share of all counts",
         subtitle = sprintf("top 20 account for %.1f%% of every count in this sample",
                            sum(.tg$pct)),
         x = NULL, y = "% of total counts") +
    theme_scratch()
}
```

```{r qc-waterfall, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.4
# Which filter removed what. A single "n cells retained" number cannot tell you
# whether a low yield came from the gene filter or the mitochondrial one, and
# those have opposite remedies.
wf <- data.table(
  step  = factor(c("input", "after gene filter", "after mito filter"),
                 levels = c("input", "after gene filter", "after mito filter")),
  cells = c(n_total_cells, n_thr_features_cells, n_observed_cells))
wf[, removed := c(0L, diff(cells)) * -1L]
wf[, tip := sprintf("%s\n%s cells%s", step, format(cells, big.mark = ","),
                    ifelse(removed > 0, sprintf("\n%s removed at this step",
                                                format(removed, big.mark = ",")), ""))]
ggplot(wf, aes(step, cells, fill = step, text = tip)) +
  geom_col(width = .6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(cells, big.mark = ",")), vjust = -.5, size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0d366b", "#3f6fa8", "#8fb4dd")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .15))) +
  labs(title = "Cells remaining after each filter",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s barcodes retained (%.1f%%)",
                          format(n_observed_cells, big.mark = ","),
                          format(n_total_cells, big.mark = ","),
                          100 * n_observed_cells / max(1, n_total_cells)),
       x = NULL, y = "cells") +
  theme_scratch()
```

```{r compile_csv}

sample_metrics_upgrade <- sample_metrics %>%
  select(`Estimated Number of Cells`, `Mean Reads per Cell`, `Median Genes per Cell`, `Median UMI Counts per Cell`, `Sequencing Saturation`) %>%
  rename(
    estimate_n_cells = `Estimated Number of Cells`,
    mean_reads_per_cell = `Mean Reads per Cell`,
    median_genes_per_cell = `Median Genes per Cell`,
    median_umi_per_cell = `Median UMI Counts per Cell`,
    seq_saturation = `Sequencing Saturation`

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_id = sample_name,
    n_total_cells = n_total_cells,
    n_thr_features_cells = n_total_cells,
    n_observed_cells = n_observed_cells,
    status_flag = status_flag
  )

sample_metrics_upgrade <- sample_metrics_upgrade %>%
    select(sample_id, status_flag, estimate_n_cells, mean_reads_per_cell, median_genes_per_cell, median_genes_per_cell, median_umi_per_cell, seq_saturation, n_total_cells, n_thr_features_cells, n_observed_cells)

write_csv(sample_metrics_upgrade, file = paste0(sample_name, '_metrics_upgrade.csv'))

```

      thr_percent_mito = thr_percent_mito,
      thr_n_observed_cells = thr_n_observed_cells,
      work_directory = work_directory,
      auto_save = auto_save
  )
)
